title: AI-assisted early detection of diseases in newborns (particularly sepsis) as well as nutrition, growth and developmental disorders in preterm and full-term infants
summary:
The NeoSepAI study investigates whether diseases in newborn infants can be detected earlier with the help of artificial intelligence. A particular focus is the early detection of neonatal sepsis. Nutrition, growth and neurological development will also be investigated.
In preterm infants and ill term-born neonates, routinely collected vital signs and selected clinical data will be recorded. These include information on pregnancy and birth, growth, nutrition, respiratory support, medication, laboratory values and clinical diagnoses. In addition, contactless video recordings will be obtained and used for automated analysis of movement, breathing patterns and skin colour.
Healthy term-born neonates will additionally be included as a reference group. Their data will be used to describe normal vital-sign, movement and growth patterns.
This is an observational study. Medical care will remain entirely according to standard clinical practice. No additional blood sampling, medication or therapeutic measures will be initiated as part of the study.
conditions: Neonatal diseases, particularly neonatal sepsis, as well as nutritional, growth and developmental disorders in preterm and term-born infants.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Preterm infant with a gestational age <37 weeks or birth weight ≤1500 g; or
ill term-born neonate (gestational age ≥37+0 weeks) treated in the neonatal unit/NICU because of an acute neonatal condition and presenting with at least one of the following: invasive or non-invasive respiratory support, clinical suspicion of sepsis with initiation of antibiotic therapy, haemodynamic instability, or another neonatal condition requiring intensive care; or
healthy term-born neonate (gestational age ≥37+0 weeks, reference group) without a need for intensive care, primarily recruited on the maternity ward; alternatively, term-born neonates who required only brief postnatal observation in the neonatal unit and rapidly stabilised without requiring intensive care.
In addition, written informed consent from the child's legal representative(s) is required.
Exclusion criteria:
No inclusion in the absence of informed consent. In addition, participants will not be included if the planned data collection is not justifiable or feasible for clinical or organisational reasons (e.g. necessary hygiene requirements or technical impossibility of camera installation), without any resulting disadvantage to clinical care.
